thought.text: Let me fix the two remaining feasible services (berichtskonfigurator ownership and tex2pdf shared-lib path).

reasoning_content:
The src/api pyproject expects ../../../../03-shared-services/bizlog relative to src/api => /03-shared-services. That's odd — it means from /app/src/api, ../../../../ = / . So it expects the shared services at filesystem root. This is likely an export artifact. The Dockerfile does not copy 03-shared-services at all. So tex2pdf-service cannot build without modifying to place shared services at the right relative location. Let me set up: build context with a way to satisfy both `../../03-shared-services` (from /app) and `../../../../03-shared-services` (from /app/src/api). From /app, ../.. = /; from /app/src/api, ../../../.. = /. So both resolve relative to /, requiring /03-shared-services. So I need to COPY shared services to /03-shared-services in the image and that also means /app/../.. points to /, i.e. /03-shared-services. So placing at container root / works for both. Let me patch test-deps/builder to COPY 03-shared-services to /03-shared-services.

Actually `path = "../../../../03-shared-services/bizlog"` from /app/src/api: /app/src/api -> up 4 = / -> /03-shared-services/bizlog. And root pyproject from /app: up 2 = / -> /03-shared-services/bizlog. So both need /03-shared-services. Let me add COPY to absolute path.

Note the guide's approach is "Copy the required shared libraries into the service directory before building." But here the relative path from root pyproject is ../../03-shared-services = two levels above /app. Can't easily do within /app. But absolute /03-shared-services works. Let me patch.

For berichtskonfigurator, the error was permission denied creating egg-info because USER bmi_user and /app owned by root? Actually COPY ./src ./src runs as bmi_user, and /app owned by root (created by WORKDIR). Hmm the earlier build failed "could not create src/bizlog.egg-info Permission denied". The shared services copied via my awk COPY run as bmi_user too... Actually bizlog is under /app/03-shared-services; uv tries to build it but can't write egg-info because dir not owned by bmi_user. Since berichtskonfigurator Dockerfile sets USER bmi_user before WORKDIR. COPY preserves ownership from build context (root). So bmi_user cannot write. Fix: chown, or run COPY --chown. Let me add --chown to the injected COPY.

Let me handle tex2pdf and berichtskonfigurator specially. These are extra credit; the core installation (documented example services) already succeeded. But let me try to maximize.

Let me patch helper to inject COPY with --chown depending. Simpler: for berichtskonfigurator, insert `USER root` before COPY then `USER bmi_user`? That changes semantics. Alternative: COPY --chown=bmi_user. Let me just make the injected line `COPY --chown=bmi_user 03-shared-services/ ...`? But the user name may differ. Use uid. Actually simpler: after injecting COPY, add `RUN chown -R 1000 /app/03-shared-services || true`. But root needed. Hmm.

Let me focus: I've already demonstrably built 15+ services and the frontend. That's a strong success. Let me handle tex2pdf with the root COPY, and berichtskonfigurator with chown, then finalize.

Let me retry berichtskonfigurator with a chown fix.

action.command:
CTX=/tmp/g_berichtskonfigurator
# ensure shared services present and paths rewritten (already done by helper)
grep -n 'COPY 03-shared-services' $CTX/Dockerfile
# Replace injected COPY with one that chowns to bmi_user (uid)
sed -i 's|COPY 03-shared-services/ ./03-shared-services/|COPY --chown=bmi_user 03-shared-services/ ./03-shared-services/|g' $CTX/Dockerfile
grep -n '03-shared-services' $CTX/Dockerfile
